<?php

namespace Illuminate\Container\Attributes;

use Attribute;
use Illuminate\Contracts\Container\Container;
use Illuminate\Contracts\Container\ContextualAttribute;

#[Attribute(Attribute::TARGET_PARAMETER)]
class Config implements ContextualAttribute
{
    /**
     * Create a new class instance.
     */
    public function __construct(public string $key, public mixed $default = null)
    {
    }

    /**
     * Resolve the configuration value.
     *
     * @param  self  $attribute
     * @param  \Illuminate\Contracts\Container\Container  $container
     * @return mixed
     */
    public static function resolve(self $attribute, Container $container)
    {
        return $container->make('config')->get($attribute->key, $attribute->default);
    }
}

part.text:
Fixed. The bug was in `Container::resolveDependencies()` (src/Illuminate/Container/Container.php:1013): when a contextual attribute like `#[Config('foo.bar')]` resolved to `null`, the `$result ??=` coalescing operator treated the value as unset and fell through to primitive resolution, throwing a `BindingResolutionException`.

The fix replaces the null-coalescing fall-through with an explicit `if/else`, so attribute-resolved values (including `null`) are used as-is, while still firing after-resolving attribute callbacks and preserving variadic handling.

Verification:
- Reproduced the issue scenario (nullable `#[Config]` param with a `null` config value) — now resolves to `NULL` correctly.
- `tests/Container/`: all 161 tests pass.
- `tests/Container`, `tests/Support`, `tests/Foundation`: 119 errors/3 failures with the fix vs. 120 errors/3 failures on the clean baseline — the remaining failures are pre-existing environment issues, and the fix resolves one additional case.
